reviews.title: So So
reviews.text: Been with Malwarebytes for many years, started with free then gradually subscriptions for the last decade. Now I have all their products on my home computers, iPad, and iPhones.  As time goes on, I have more questions than answers, it has become a less user-friendly app, instructions are less intuitive, and the number of products increases without them letting you know if you already bought one of their services. I have paid for the same services more than once. They are happy to take multiple payments even though I already own the product/service. Installation instructions and the sequencing of installation is often unclear and unnecessarily redundant. My confidence level in Malwarebytes has diminished over time! Customer service has decreased over time. They advertise their availability but I never received the help I needed even when a live person was contacted. They acted like I was a bother because I couldn’t figure out their instructions. But it wasn’t me that was the problem; it was this company staff member who didn’t have the expertise or patience to talk/walk me through it.

reviews.title: Fake ads for evil, useless product
reviews.text:
The ads for this app show a woman using Malwarebytes to remove malware from her iPhone, after which it stops running slow and overheating.

The very first thing the App Store description says is that this is a powerful “antivirus”.

And of course the entire value of the name “Malwarebytes” is that people have heard that it can scan for and remove viruses and other malware on their Windows desktop machines. So that’s obviously what they’d expect the iOS version of the app with the same name and same logo to do, even if it weren’t being explicitly advertised that way.

I was curious how they could possibly do any of this on iOS, with the sandbox.

The answer is: they don’t. The main feature they’re advertising is impossible, so they just don’t do it.

So, what do they do? The app doesn’t include the actual Malwarebytes product, but it does include all the other add-on stuff they try to upsell you with when you install Malwarebytes. Most of which you won’t need, much of which you won’t want—but, more importantly, none of it is what they advertise.

Plus, you can’t even get into the app without signing up for a free trial—and then they pile on all the usual scammer annoyances to make it as hard as possible for you to cancel before the trial ends. So the app is, itself, malware.

What do you call a program whose main purpose is to trick you into purchasing a subscription that you don’t want and that you will not know how to cancel? I know what Martin Kleczynski and Malwarebytes wo

: How our free version would work is if you have already used the trial, it would skip this step and automatically install the free scanner version.  If it is giving you the option to start a trial, you would have to do this step in order for it to revert to the free version after the free 7-day trial.  It does require you to enter billing info but you can immediately cancel this or ask us to do this for you and then you get the free premium features for 7 days, after that it will just be our completely free remediation version.

1. nothing was said about any requirements or limitations using the software for free.

3. I still don’t understand what they told me in that text.
